- assessment_id: COORD-CASE-11
  area: scope
  topic: Independent complete source-case/proposal review with retained scientific
    limits
  outcome: supported
  summary: Coordinator read current complete target and its source/payload delta;
    provenance, before-image/history, native shape and explicit hold retention checked.
    The origin peer conclusion below is attributed, not a new release approval.
  details: 'Attributed origin assessment: All seven occurrences denote filtered natural
    seawater as an input before mixing or autoclaving. CCAP MErds/NSS low require
    filling to one litre with it; MY75S and ZM10 explicitly dilute that input. NSS
    low and 2SNA allow synthetic salt alternatives, which remain separate alternatives.
    This scoped input is consistent with the Filtered Seawater owner; final-medium
    dilution and autoclaving do not turn its input label into a different source ingredient.
    Final-review qualification of the historical #260 dilution rationale: the original
    CCAP PE footnote explicitly says to filter natural seawater, reduce it to 95%
    using glass distilled water, and autoclave. That prepared input is then dosed
    at 950 cm3; the prior dilution is not inferred from the receiving-medium dose.
    The literal 95%-strength label is retained as REJECTED_LABEL on this bare filtered-seawater
    owner, without inventing the percentage basis, final volume, component ratio or
    a new preparation owner. The unqualified Natural seawater alias is also nonresolving:
    its recovered JCM1377 contexts state natural seawater without filtration. Supported
    Filtered natural seawater and Natural seawater (filtrated) aliases remain. Earlier
    #260 mapping evidence and histories are preserved as historical rationale, superseded
    only on these alias applicability points by this source-backed qualification.

    20 mM. The newly inspected Coppi2001 FWAFC methods specify 55.9 mM Fe(III) citrate
    and print 13.7 g FeC6O7/L; Risso2009 culture methods specify ferric citrate 56
    mM. These recovered ferric-citrate inputs do not establish the shared two-ligand
    CHEBI:4991 ion or validate KEGG:fe3dcit as a KEGG compound accession. Labarre1987
    pp4668–4669 and Anderson1991 pp2761–2762 name BG11 and modifications without specifying
    the citrate reagent in those inspected methods. Park2005 supplied an explicit
    subscription preview rather than methods; its Europe PMC request timed out. Shcolnick2007
    metadata/abstract was read, while the ScienceDirect full-article route returned
    HTTP403/CPE00001. The referenced Rippka1979 full-text route returned HTTP403 with
    a JavaScript/cookie challenge. These are route-specific limits, not a blanket
    claim that primary methods are unavailable. The exact shared dicitrate association
    remains held pending per-occurrence source-to-model identity reconciliation; neither
    one freshwater formulation nor an unverified BG11 recipe may be applied to all

  details: 'Attributed origin assessment: NBRC 355 directs adding HCl to warmed milk
    to coagulate it, centrifuging, and using the supernatant as cheese whey. The source-defined
    output can be represented without a quantified yield. Starting milk and HCl are
    processing inputs; precipitated milk proteins are removed, and their masses or
    final retained fractions are not asserted as has-part components. Applies only
    to CultureMech 015901/nbrc.medium 355 in case 23. DSMZ 775 and JCM 162 name cheese
    whey as the liquid substrate without the NBRC 355 acid-coagulation preparation.
